_comment: Tileable surface textures. Same provenance rule as fixtures/manifest.json: these files ship inside client deliverables, so CC0 only and every entry carries its source. Unlike the fixture assets, these are kept at their source tone -- the tint that reaches the render comes from mesh_builder's measured _PALETTE, applied at load time, so the palette stays the single authority on colour and these files stay as-downloaded apart from the resize noted below.

oak_floor.author: Lennart Demes / ambientCG
oak_floor.licence_verified: ambientCG is CC0 site-wide; confirmed on the asset page before download
oak_floor.modifications: 1K Color map, resized 1024x1024 -> 512x512 (Lanczos) and re-encoded JPEG q82.
oak_floor.native_map_set: Color, Roughness, NormalDX, NormalGL, Displacement, AmbientOcclusion
oak_floor.tile_note: Physical tile size is a judgement, not published by the source: 1200mm across ~6 visible planks gives ~200mm plank width, which is realistic wide-plank oak and matches the reference proposal's floor scale.
oak_floor.selection_note: Chosen over WoodFloor051 (the manifest's own backup) after rendering both: 051 is a mid-brown parquet, mean RGB (155,123,93), far darker than the tone measured off the reference render. 039's long planks and light warm tone match page 3.

orm.packing: R=AmbientOcclusion, G=Roughness, B=0 (non-metal). Standard glTF ORM packing -- one image serves both metallicRoughnessTexture and occlusionTexture, per the glTF spec's own note that this is a common optimization.
orm.source_maps: 1K Roughness + 1K AmbientOcclusion, resized to match the colour map, re-encoded JPEG q85.

normal.source_map: 1K NormalGL, resized to match the colour map, re-encoded JPEG q90 with 4:4:4 chroma (no subsampling) -- subsampling blurs the G/B channels that encode tangent-space X/Y and visibly misdirects the lighting.

concrete_wall.author: Lennart Demes / ambientCG
concrete_wall.licence_verified: ambientCG is CC0 site-wide; confirmed on the asset page before download
concrete_wall.modifications: 1K Color map, resized 1024x512 -> 512x256 (Lanczos, aspect preserved) and re-encoded JPEG q82.
concrete_wall.tile_note: Source map is 2:1, so the world tile is too; 2400mm across reads as a broad cast-concrete panel rather than a repeating pattern.

orm.packing: R=255 (Concrete034 ships no AmbientOcclusion map -- flat, i.e. no occlusion), G=Roughness, B=0 (non-metal).
orm.source_maps: 1K Roughness only, resized to match the colour map, re-encoded JPEG q85.

normal.source_map: 1K NormalGL, resized to match the colour map, re-encoded JPEG q90 with 4:4:4 chroma (no subsampling).

Wood028.intended_use: matte black laminate for cabinet and counter bodies
Wood028.reason_not_shipped: Deliberately skipped, not overlooked. The candidate manifest that sourced it recorded fit_quality 'rough' and its own note said a flat near-black -- already in the measured palette -- would likely read better at massing-model viewing distance than a wood-category material merely tagged 'black'. Cabinetry in the reference is a uniform matte near-black with no visible grain, so a wood texture there would add error, not detail. Revisit only if a real laminate scan becomes available.
Wood028.roughness_handled_instead: The flatness complaint it was meant to answer is addressed by giving every material a real roughnessFactor rather than the previous blanket 1.0.

shipped_since.roughness_and_normal_maps: Previously withheld pending an eye-level walk mode (see git history for the prior note). Now shipped for floor and wall -- the two textured materials -- as packed ORM + normal JPEGs, ~48KB added per material. Still only these two: a 100mm-deep fixture band shows too little of a tile for a normal map to read, so cabinetry etc. stay scalar-roughness flat colour.
